note.text:
A pure substance is made of only one kind of matter. It is either an element (iron, oxygen, gold) or a compound (water, table salt, sugar, carbon dioxide). It has fixed melting and boiling points.
A mixture contains two or more substances that are not chemically joined. Each keeps its own properties, and they can be separated by physical methods (filtering, evaporating, distilling…). Examples: air, sea water, soil, tap water, palm wine, a soft drink, concrete, milk.
The amounts in a mixture can vary: tea can be weak or strong. The make-up of a pure substance never varies: water is always hydrogen and oxygen in the same ratio.

worked_example.problem: Is sea water a pure substance or a mixture? How do you know?
steps: Sea water contains water and dissolved salts.
If you let it evaporate, the salt is left behind: the parts were separated by a physical method.
Its saltiness varies from place to place.

cards.idea: A pure substance is one kind of matter only: an element or a compound. It has fixed melting and boiling points.
example: Distilled water, table salt, oxygen, gold.

cards.idea: A mixture has two or more substances, not chemically joined, that can be separated by physical methods.
example: Sea water: evaporate the water and the salt is left.

cards.idea: The amounts in a mixture can vary; in a pure substance they are fixed.
example: Tea can be weak or strong; water is always H₂O.

check.prompt: Which sentence is about a mixture?

right.text: Its parts can be present in any amounts.

wrong.text: It has a fixed boiling point.
It is made of only one kind of matter.
It can only be split by a chemical reaction.
wrong.explain: Mixtures can be separated by physical methods.

questions.prompt: Sort them: pure substance or mixture?
Which of these is a mixture?

wrong.explain: Distilled water is one kind of matter only: a pure substance.
Table salt (sodium chloride) is one kind of matter only: a pure substance.
Sugar is one kind of matter only: a pure substance.
Oxygen is one kind of matter only: a pure substance.
Iron is one kind of matter only: a pure substance.
Gold is one kind of matter only: a pure substance.
Carbon dioxide is one kind of matter only: a pure substance.

questions.prompt: Why is air a mixture and not a pure substance?

right.text: It contains several gases (nitrogen, oxygen, carbon dioxide…) that are not chemically joined.

wrong.explain: We cannot see oxygen either, and oxygen is pure.
Oxygen is a gas and it is pure.
That does not decide; air is several gases mixed together.

questions.prompt: One sentence is wrong. Which one?

right.text: The parts of a mixture can be separated by physical methods.

wrong.text: Tap water is a pure substance.
wrong.explain: Tap water contains dissolved substances: it is a mixture.

wrong.text: A mixture has a fixed boiling point.
wrong.explain: Mixtures boil over a range of temperatures.
